I didn’t start in Learning & Development with a big toolkit or expensive software. I started with free AI tools. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini — all open at the same time. NotebookLM for structuring, breaking down, and making sense of content. Synthesia for my very first gig — I used a free Synthesia link as a video intro. Canva for visuals. A lot of curiosity and a willingness to figure things out as I went. What surprised me most wasn’t how “advanced” the tools were — it was how quickly they helped me think differently about learning design. From lesson planning → to learning experiences. From content creation → to learning journeys. From teaching delivery → to learner-centered design. For teachers transitioning into Learning & Development, you already have the core skill set: ✔ explaining complex ideas simply ✔ understanding how people learn ✔ adapting in real time ✔ designing for engagement (even if you didn’t call it that yet) The shift isn’t about starting over. It’s about translating what you already do into a new context. And yes — AI can help accelerate that translation. Not replace your thinking, but expand what you can create with limited time and resources. If you’re a teacher exploring L&D: Start small. Use free tools. Experiment often. Build as you learn. You don’t need permission to begin — just a starting point. #LearningAndDevelopment #InstructionalDesign l #TeachersInTransition #EdTech #ArtificialIntelligence #NotebookLM #Synthesia #Canva #FutureOfWork #ProfessionalDevelopment
